clue.text: Follows a sailor to get navigational aid

parts.note: to dog someone is to follow them closely
tar is an old word for a sailor

explanation.surface: Someone tails a seaman hoping he will help them find their way.
explanation.walkthrough: Sailors once steered by the Dog Star, Sirius, the brightest star in the night sky.
explanation.definitionFit: Sirius, the brightest star, served sailors as a guide for steering at night.

clue.text: Store silicon in a warehouse

indicators.note: the element's symbol is placed inside the word for a storehouse

parts.note: a depot is a storehouse
Si is the chemical symbol for silicon

explanation.surface: Keep a stock of silicon chips in a warehouse.
explanation.definitionFit: To deposit something is to put it away somewhere for safe keeping.

clue.text: Prepare to play ice hockey and make it snappy

explanation.surface: Advice to an ice hockey player who is dawdling before the game.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally a hockey player laces up blades before playing; idiomatically the phrase means hurry up.

clue.text: Where travellers for Teesside are bound to find quality

parts.note: travellers heading for a place are going to it
Teesside lies in the North East of England, abbreviated NE

explanation.surface: Asks where people heading to Teesside will find something good.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole phrase 'Where travellers for Teesside are bound' reads as TO NE: to the North East, the English region (round Middlesbrough) that contains Teesside.
explanation.definitionFit: Tone is the character or quality of a sound, voice or colour.

clue.text: Begin once more to produce pictures after a break

indicators.note: the word for pictures comes after the word for a break

parts.note: a rest is a break from work
paintings and drawings are art

explanation.surface: An artist returns to painting after a pause.
explanation.definitionFit: To restart is to start again after stopping.

clue.text: A physician should, when water is scarce

parts.note: Dr is the abbreviation for a doctor
ought means should

explanation.surface: A doctor's advice on what one ought to do during a water shortage.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a descriptive phrase for a long dry spell rather than a strict synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: A drought is a long spell without rain, leaving water in short supply.

clue.text: Leave school early to go parachuting

explanation.surface: A teenager quits school to take up skydiving.
explanation.definitionFit: To quit education before finishing is to drop out; parachutists literally fall out of a plane.

clue.text: In Samoa they swear by it

indicators.note: the word sits inside the run of letters across the two words

explanation.surface: Islanders in the Pacific have something they hold sacred.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across Samoa and they: samOA THey.
explanation.definitionFit: A solemn promise is made by swearing on something, typically a holy book.

clue.text: Maybe the ADC will take on any job

definitions.text: Maybe the ADC will take on any job

parts.words: Maybe the ADC will take on any job
parts.note: an ADC, aide-de-camp, is the personal assistant to a senior officer, a general's do-everything helper

explanation.surface: An aide-de-camp willing to do whatever task is going.
explanation.walkthrough: ADC stands for aide-de-camp, an officer assisting a general: so he is a general's factotum, while the phrase also means a person who does all sorts of jobs.
explanation.definitionFit: A factotum is a servant or employee who handles every kind of task.

clue.text: Eat nuts in a stew, and illness will result

indicators.note: something in a stew is in a muddle, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Eating nuts cooked in a casserole will make you ill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stew' suggests cooking but signals that EATNUTS is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Lockjaw is a serious bacterial infection causing muscle spasms.

clue.text: Blunder about the way to utilise a mule

definitions.text: about the way to utilise a mule

explanation.surface: Someone makes a mistake while thinking about how to use a pack animal.
explanation.walkthrough: A mule here is not the animal but a backless slipper, which you wear by inserting your foot.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to say something tactless; a slipper is used by sliding a foot inside.

clue.text: Pretentious cobbler

explanation.surface: A shoemaker who gives himself airs.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition 'Pretentious' is loose: it describes the kind of person rather than naming them. Snob is an old dialect word for a shoemaker.
explanation.definitionFit: A snooty social climber is pretentious; the word also once meant a shoe-mender.

clue.text: Has the ability to get on in the Church

parts.note: can means is able to

explanation.surface: Someone has the talent to advance in a clerical career.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Get on in the Church' reads as climbing the clergy ladder, a pleasing misdirection since a canon is also a clergyman.
explanation.definitionFit: Canon means church law, a body of rules laid down by a church council.

clue.text: Jenny has joined the Navy

explanation.surface: A woman named Jenny has enlisted as a sailor.
explanation.walkthrough: Jenny wren is a traditional name for the small bird; a Wren was a member of the Women's Royal Naval Service.
explanation.definitionFit: The little songbird is nicknamed jenny, and women in the Royal Navy were called after the service's initials.

clue.text: Sharedthecannabis smoker's cigarette

explanation.surface: People passed round a cannabis cigarette.
explanation.definitionFit: A joint effort is shared; a hand-rolled marijuana cigarette is also called this.

clue.text: Southern hypocrisy achieves very little

parts.note: cant is insincere pious talk

explanation.surface: Hypocrisy in the South gets nowhere.
explanation.definitionFit: Scant means barely sufficient, hardly any.

clue.text: Get up and dress

explanation.surface: Instructions to rise from bed and put clothes on.
explanation.definitionFit: To turn out is to rise or assemble; a turnout is also an outfit or way of dressing.

clue.text: Credit to Leslie for the light touches

parts.note: on tick means on credit
Les is short for Leslie

explanation.surface: Leslie gets the credit for some deft finishing work.
explanation.walkthrough: Buying 'on tick' is British slang for buying on credit.
explanation.definitionFit: A feather or fingertip brushed lightly over the skin causes this sensation.

clue.text: Admitted that one was gullible

explanation.surface: Someone confesses to being easily fooled.
explanation.definitionFit: Being let in means admitted; being fooled or deceived is the gullible sense.

clue.text: On the way for a hospital visit

parts.note: heading for somewhere is going to it
hospital rooms for patients are wards

explanation.surface: Travelling to visit someone in hospital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'For a hospital visit' reads as going to the wards of a hospital.
explanation.definitionFit: Towards means in the direction of something.

clue.text: No colliery has a key candidate

parts.note: a colliery is a coal mine
E is a musical key

explanation.surface: A colliery lacks a key person to put forward.
explanation.definitionFit: A nominee is a person put forward for election or an award.

clue.text: The answer appears in a solid parliamentary report

indicators.note: the abbreviation for answer sits inside the word for solid

parts.note: hard means solid
ans is the abbreviation for answer

explanation.surface: A solution turns up in a robust account of debates.
explanation.walkthrough: Hansard is the official verbatim record of the UK Parliament's debates.
explanation.definitionFit: The official printed record of Westminster debates is named after its first printer.

clue.text: Lance, keep talking about love

indicators.note: the phrase for nagging goes around the letter for love

parts.note: to harp on is to keep talking about something
O is love, a zero score in tennis

explanation.surface: Lance is told to keep going on about romance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lance' looks like a man's name but is the spear-like weapon definition; O (love) goes inside HARP ON.
explanation.definitionFit: A barbed spear thrown at whales is a kind of lance.

clue.text: Prison debt-collector meets George before noon

parts.note: a dun is someone who demands payment of debts

explanation.surface: A debt collector has a meeting with George in the morning.
explanation.definitionFit: A dungeon is an underground cell in a castle for holding captives.

clue.text: Hardliners regard them as drips

parts.note: a drip is a feeble person; Thatcher-era hardliners dismissed moderate Tories with a word for feeble and soggy

explanation.surface: Hardliners look down on feeble people.
explanation.walkthrough: In 1980s British politics Margaret Thatcher's hardline supporters called moderate Conservatives by a word meaning feeble.
explanation.definitionFit: Moderate Tories were nicknamed so by Thatcherites, the word also meaning feeble, ineffectual people.

clue.text: Backing electrically-powered vehicles proves astute

indicators.note: backing means going backwards, so the vehicles' word is read from the end

parts.note: trams are electrically powered vehicles on rails

explanation.surface: Investing in electric vehicles turns out to be a clever move.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Backing' looks like financial support but signals that TRAMS is read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Smart means quick-witted and shrewd.

clue.text: It educates in the English style

parts.note: ton is fashion or style, as in the phrase bon ton

explanation.surface: A school teaches in an English fashion.
explanation.walkthrough: Eton is a famous English private school; 'ton' is an old word for high fashion.
explanation.definitionFit: Eton College is a famous boarding school near Windsor.

clue.text: A weapon used by President Eisenhower

parts.note: Ike was the nickname of President Dwight Eisenhower

explanation.surface: A weapon wielded by President Eisenhower.
explanation.definitionFit: A pike is a long infantry spear.

clue.text: Spoil a fine act

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for fine, as on pencils
an act of parliament is a law

explanation.surface: A good piece of work is ruined.
explanation.definitionFit: To flaw something is to mar it with a defect.

clue.text: Obstruction in a Soviet highway can be suicidal

indicators.note: the obstruction word goes inside the highway words

parts.note: a Russian route is a Soviet road
a let is a hindrance, as in without let or hindrance

explanation.surface: A roadblock on a Soviet road may prove deadly.
explanation.walkthrough: LET goes into RUSSIAN ROUTE. The definition is loose: the game is one that can be suicidal.
explanation.definitionFit: In this deadly game a player spins a revolver's cylinder with one bullet and pulls the trigger.

clue.text: Carved screen I regard as genuine

indicators.note: carved means cut into a new shape, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone admires an ornately carved screen as authentic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Carved' suggests woodwork but signals that SCREEN and I are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Sincere means honest and without pretence.

clue.text: Journalist sends an old cardinal round the bend

indicators.note: the cardinal's name goes round the letter shaped like a bend

parts.note: John Henry Newman was a nineteenth-century cardinal
S is the shape of a bend, as in an S-bend

explanation.surface: A reporter drives an elderly churchman crazy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Round the bend' means mad, but here Cardinal Newman goes round S, the S-bend.
explanation.definitionFit: A newsman is a reporter or journalist.
